outcomeNote: A list of Rav Yehuda's with a baraita's variant and two anonymous additions; no argument.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁלֹשָׁה צְרִיכִין שִׁימּוּר, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן — חוֹלֶה, חָתָן, וְכַלָּה. בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: חוֹלֶה, חַיָּה, חָתָן, וְכַלָּה. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף אָבֵל. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בַּלַּיְלָה.
segments.en: Incidental to Rav Yehuda’s earlier statement, which organized several cases into a single category, the Gemara cites similar statements of his. «Rav Yehuda said: Three require protection» from harm: «A sick person, a bridegroom, and a bride. It was taught in a baraita: A sick person, a woman in childbirth, a bridegroom, and a bride» require protection from harm. «And some say: Even a mourner. And some say: Even Torah scholars at night.» Those whose thoughts are focused elsewhere or are in a weakened physical state require protection.
